messages:
ana: FYI on Orion-INT4 bring-up: saw structured funcall failures after enabling cross-request batching in the serving pool. Baseline ~0.3% -> 3.8% after the change.

ana: Raw example (copied from logs):
```
{"tool":"db_fetch","args":{"user":42},"result":{"email":"x@ex.com"}}
```

maria: timeline? which rollout and which batching knob did you flip?

ana: rolled orion-int4:v0.9 to canary (10%) and enabled cross_request_batching=true, batch_window=15ms. Canary started 2024-11-06T14:12:00Z.

kevin: Cross-request batching + quantized kernels can reorder token emission at stream boundaries. That \u0003 control char smells like kernel-side sentinel leaking.

sasha: quick checks: 1) run same canary with batch_window=0 (no cross-request merge) 2) run with streaming=false 3) run against dedicated pool (no shared kvcache)

deploy-bot: canary deploy: orion-int4 v0.9 -> 10% @ 2024-11-06T14:12:00Z. autoscale: ok.

ana: ran three probes (1k each): batch_window=15ms parse_fail=3.8%, batch_window=0 parse_fail=0.5%, streaming_off parse_fail=0.6%. Link: https://console.redwood/evals/orion-int4/1746660000

raj: sounds like the merge path is the culprit. Can you capture tokenizer offsets + logits around EOF for a sample of failures? need to see if token boundary split caused the control char.

kevin: also try launching a build with kernel flag strip_stream_ctrl=true or suppress_stream_sentinals=true. If kernel emits them, compilation flag should fix.

ana: queued a build with strip_stream_ctrl and will run a 1k micro-canary with batch_window=15ms, streaming on.

maria: in parallel add a client-side tolerant parser that does: try json.loads, if fail -> rstrip non-JSON until last closing brace, then reparse; count rescue rate and attach telemetry tag "rescue.rstrip_eof". Also add a retry that forces single-request processing for rescued calls.

ana: implemented rescue patch and deployed as a runtime hotfix to the canary: immediate rescue reduced visible errors to 1.2% (from 3.8%), but we should still fix root cause upstream.

eval-bot: sampled_failures: 38/1000 (batch15ms), rescued=26/38 via rstrip, failures_remaining=12. Artifacts: samples/1746660000/fails.tar.gz

kevin: good telemetry. if strip_stream_ctrl build returns parse_fail near baseline in micro-canary, we can promote. If not, isolate further (kvcache flush at request boundary).

sasha: one more thought: add an explicit end-sentinel to funcall contract (e.g. "__END_FUNC_CALL__") so parsers can be deterministic even under streaming. Might be a protocol-level change though.

raj: agree it's heavy-handed but robust. For now prefer kernel flag + client rescue + dedicated-pool test.

ana: plan: 1) run strip_stream_ctrl micro-canary (results in ~40m) 2) run dedicated-pool batch test 3) leave rescue parser in place and monitor rescue.rate and latency impact 4) if we keep streaming long-term, propose end-sentinel RFC.

maria: +1 on plan. tagging oncall for monitoring dashboards and adding "eof_ctrlchar" telemetry slice.

ana: will post micro-canary numbers when ready. thanks :thumbsup:
__note: messages must be a single continuous string; title omitted per agents.md
